comparisons.finding: Best browsing structure: titles and quieter date/outcome lines scan cleanly at both sizes. Detail has a clear heading, Back and prominent outcome button. Ledger rows need a stronger visible opening affordance.
Disclosure arrows make expansion explicit and retain neighboring records. Equal emphasis on title, date and outcome creates cumbersome multiline summaries at 200%; the outcome action looks secondary.
Selected claim and outcome button are clear, but the selector conceals the history overview. At 200%, the selected record title is visibly truncated and has no full heading elsewhere.
Strongest claim-to-choice sequence. Original question stays secondary; selected radio, saved message and Saved button agree. At 200%, Save requires scrolling but is fully visible at the end.
Compact choices come at the cost of hiding the claim being evaluated. Opening the full reference at 200% pushes choices far down. Selection and saved confirmation remain visually clear.

Persistent saved feedback is prominent, but entry adds a Record outcome step. At 200%, the footer limits the visible choices; Not yet appears only after scrolling. End capture shows it remains reachable.

Explicit index links, section headings and return links support continuous reading. At 200%, the index consumes substantial space and long paragraphs separate sections widely; navigation remains visibly available.

Best section discovery: all four subjects are immediately visible with consistent disclosure cues. Expanded answers read cleanly at 200%, with remaining sections accessible below. Long content still requires scrolling.

Focused section reading and large previous/next controls work visually. Selector hides the section inventory; navigation lacks destination names or position, and Previous appears active on the first shown section.

Generous writing width, visible count updates and a clear focused outline. Before focus, text resembles read-only prose; at 200%, the invisible field boundary makes internal clipping harder to interpret.

Best editor grouping: bordered input, character count and Done stay together. Focus and draft changes are visible. At 200%, the field scrolls internally with partial lines; Back's treatment of edits is unspecified.
Explicit Cancel and Done clarify the command choices, with a well-defined input and focus ring. The detached footer separates commands from the counter; 200% text requires internal field scrolling.

Best comparison: all three prices and billing summaries are exposed. Checkmark and simulation-button wording track the selected plan. At 200%, comparison requires scrolling but retains readable prices and terms.
Selected price, terms and action form a compact group, and yearly selection is clear. The selector hides competing prices and savings, making comparison depend on remembering successive offers.

Collapsed rows expose all headline prices, but opening and selecting are visually entangled. Initially, the weekly action implies selection without a matching row marker. Expanded yearly detail repeats its price.

Best overview and detail hierarchy: destination summaries preview content, while the shared forecast gets its own heading and Back. Both sizes remain readable. Destination rows need clearer navigation cues.
Selector keeps the page short but hides available destinations. People appear as one dense paragraph mixing names, handles, signs and permissions; enlarged text amplifies the weak grouping.

Consistent disclosure rows make destinations discoverable and retain context around the shared forecast. Initial view offers no content previews; at 200%, expanded content pushes controls toward the scroll boundary.

reason: Prefer visible comparisons for records and prices, the exact claim beside outcome choices, discoverable disclosures for evidence, and a clearly bounded editor with adjacent commands. Circle A wins narrowly for useful previews and distinct detail hierarchy. Scores assess the supplied compositions and visible component states; none establishes the full acceptance threshold.
limitations: Independent review of the attached sheets only; no source, earlier reviews, runtime inspection or checks.json inspection.

Accessibility scores cover visible enlargement, wrapping, control presentation and content reachability only. Target dimensions, measured contrast, keyboard behavior, focus restoration, screen readers and reduced motion are unverified.
Feedback scores cover depicted selection, draft-count and saved-label changes only. Null means feedback/recovery was not sufficiently established; no error recovery or persistence is proven.
Only 390px sheets were inspected. Broader width checks and exercised actions are user-reported evidence, not independently reproduced.

Synthetic prototypes do not establish real storage, billing, social transport, model results, native behavior or performance. Missing physical-device proof is recorded separately rather than used as a blanket score penalty.
Screen scores do not certify every component. Findings identify component strengths and defects; no full browser or native 9/10 certification is established.
